subject: Subprocessor notice cadence + DPA e-sign cutover plan (BigFintech)
messages:
From: Martin Lee <martin.lee@bigfintech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BigFintech Procurement <procurement@bigfintech.com>, Olivia Ramos <olivia.ramos@bigfintech.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Subprocessor notice cadence and DPA execution timing

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput numbers. Before procurement can greenlight the contract, we need clarity on two items: 1) your subprocessor notification cadence and objection process (our security team needs assurance of a minimum notice window and a clear escalation path), and 2) which e-sign provider you plan to use for the DPA (we need DocuSign audit trail + signature evidence).

Can you confirm whether Redwood will commit to a 30- or 45-day notification window for new subprocessors, outline the objection matrix, and confirm the DocuSign envelope workflow? Procurement would like a single point of contact on this thread.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement has a week to finalize.

Best,
Martin
Martin Lee
Head of Security Programs, BigFintech
martin.lee@bigfintech.com
+1 415 555 0123
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Martin Lee <martin.lee@bigfintech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor notice cadence and DPA execution timing

Hi Martin — thanks for the clear ask and great questions. Putting a concise plan below so procurement has what it needs: 

1) Notification window: we propose a 45-day advance written notice for changes that materially affect data handling (new subprocessors with access to customer data). For low-risk infra-only changes (e.g., switching CDN provider without access to customer keys), we will notify at least 15 days in advance and publish to the customer portal.

2) Objection process: customers have 30 days from notice to raise objections with supporting rationale. If an objection is raised, we will:
  - pause onboarding of the subprocessor for that customer
  - provide mitigation details and any compensating controls within 7 business days
  - if unresolved, escalate to an internal review board (technical + legal) with expected resolution within 21 calendar days.

3) DPA signature / e-sign: Redwood will use DocuSign for all DPA executions with a visible audit trail. We can provide the DocuSign envelope ID and a PDF of the signed DPA.

4) Evidence: we will attach the current subprocessor list and a SOC 2 summary page; full SOC 2 report can be shared under an NDA if required.

Attachments included: subprocessor_list_20261101.csv, DPA_Redline_BigFintech_v3.docx (redline), DocuSign_authorization.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm BigFintech is OK with the 45-day notice plus the 30-day objection window? If you prefer a 30-day notice we can outline a comms/compensating-control package to shorten the window for specific categories. I’ll loop in Legal for any redline follow-ups.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor notice cadence and DPA execution timing

Vanessa — quick internal note. 45 days is conservative and preferred for compliance; however customers will push for 30 in commercial deals. If BigFintech insists on 30 we should: 

  - Offer a 30-day notice for subprocessors that are assessed as low-to-medium risk in our vendor scoring matrix (we can publish the score and key controls).
  - Retain 45-day notice for any subprocessor that handles customer data, keys, or PII.
  - Add an explicit escalation point to Legal (karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com) and Product Security (rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com) to ensure timely remediation.

If we grant 30 across-the-board, request approval from Legal and Security for a one-off concession template.

—Karthik
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor notice cadence and DPA execution timing

Adding Compliance itemization for BigFintech procurement: 

A) Audit artifacts required prior to signature:
  - SOC 2 Type II summary + date range (we can provide summary; full report on NDA)
  - DocuSign envelope audit trail (timestamps, signer IPs) attached to executed DPA
  - Subprocessor due diligence summary (security questionnaire results, vendor score) for all subprocessors with access to customer data

B) Data transfer and controls:
  - Confirm whether any subprocessors will be outside EU for EU customers (not relevant here, BigFintech is US).
  - Clarify encryption at rest and in transit and KMS boundaries for dedicated deployments (if requested).

C) Record retention: provide retention schedule for audit logs and how long we retain subprocessor notices.

I can prepare a one-page evidence pack to attach to the DocuSign envelope (SOC2 summary + subproc due diligence matrix + retention policy). If legal needs the full SOC2 we’ll route under NDA.

-Neha
Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Martin Lee <martin.lee@bigfintech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BigFintech Procurement <procurement@bigfintech.com>, Olivia Ramos <olivia.ramos@bigfintech.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor notice cadence and DPA execution timing

Vanessa — thanks for the detail. Procurement reviewed your proposed approach. A few notes: 

  - BigFintech prefers a 30-day notice as a baseline. We’ll accept 45 for high-risk data-access subprocessors but want the ability to treat a given subprocessor as high-risk only with documented rationale.
  - We need the DocuSign envelope audit trail included in the executed package; please attach the PDF audit report.
  - The DPA redline contains two small changes: an explicit 30-day objection window clause and a requirement that Redwood provide the subprocessor due diligence summary upon notice. I attached our procurement memo (procurement_note_BF.pdf) with track changes.

If you can accept those two redlines, procurement will sign and we can complete the DocuSign flow this week.

Thanks,
Martin
(attachment: procurement_note_BF.pdf)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Martin Lee <martin.lee@bigfintech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor notice cadence and DPA execution timing

Martin — good progress. We accepted the two redlines as described: 1) baseline 30-day notice for low/medium-risk subprocessors with 45-day default for any subprocessor that accesses customer data or keys; 2) commit to include a due diligence summary with the notice. Legal has prepared the updated DPA (attached).

I’ve initiated the DocuSign envelope (link below) containing: executed DPA, SOC2 summary (one-page), subprocessor list CSV, and the DocuSign audit trail placeholder. Once BigFintech signs we’ll attach the full DocuSign audit report and the final subproc due diligence summary.

Vanessa Ortiz
